direct_claims: This chart reports the share of the population living in multidimensional poverty across countries.
The subject is multidimensional poverty rather than income poverty alone.
The provided domain definition states that multidimensional poverty means being deprived in a range of health, education and living standards indicators.
The source is Our World in Data, and the chart cites Alkire et al. (2025) and the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index 2025.
The map uses each country's most recent available household survey estimate between 2013 and 2023 rather than a single common reference year for all countries.
In this dataset, the value for each country is a percentage share of people experiencing overlapping deprivations, not just a count of people below an income threshold.
The metadata indicates that countries are represented using their most recent survey year, so differences between countries may reflect both real conditions and differences in survey timing.
This data matters because multidimensional poverty captures shortages in basic capabilities and living conditions, not only low income.
The chart is not suitable for measuring change over time within countries because the provided figure uses each country's latest available survey rather than a consistent annual series.
A separate dataset is noted as being produced to monitor trends over time.
The provided metadata is incomplete because five additional rows are truncated, so any ranking statement here applies only to the visible rows unless supported by the image text.
The image also indicates that some countries have no data.
